automatically","depth":"standard"}},{"kind":"text","text":"## Which framework wins?

**Vercel’s public documentation does not specify a tie-break order for conflicting framework markers**—for example, whether a root `package.json` dependency on `next` beats a root `vite.config.ts` and `index.html`. So the marker list alone does **not** establish a documented “Next.js always wins” or “Vite always wins” rule.

What the docs do establish is the configuration precedence:

1. **Automatic detection supplies defaults** for builds and deployments.
2. **The project’s Framework Preset** in Dashboard → **Settings → Build & Deployment** is used for deployments in that project. You can select the preset yourself.
3. **`framework` in `vercel.json` can override the dashboard preset for a specific deployment.** Vercel requires a valid framework slug; `null` selects **Other**. `vite` and `nextjs` are valid slugs.

Thus, for a repository containing both sets of markers in the same detected project root, don’t rely on an undocumented detector tie-break. Set the intended preset explicitly. Vercel describes its automatic framework defaults and dashboard selection in [Configuring a Build](https://vercel.com/docs/builds/configure-a-build), and documents the `framework` override and supported values in [Programmatic Configuration with `vercel.ts`](https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/vercel-ts). The static JSON configuration uses the same framework setting; the build docs specifically direct users to `vercel.json` for a per-deployment override.

### Fix steps

**For a project-wide choice:**

1. Open the Vercel project.
2. Go to **Settings → Build & Deployment**.
3. Under **Framework Settings**, set **Framework Preset** to **Next.js** or **Vite**.
4. Save and redeploy. Vercel says the selected preset applies to all deployments in that project. Check the deployment details/build logs to confirm the framework and build settings.

**For a repository-defined, per-deployment choice**, put this at the project root in `vercel.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json",
  "framework": "vite"
}
```

Use `"nextjs"` for Next.js, or `"framework": null` for **Other**. Make sure this file is at the root Vercel uses for that project.

**If the apps are in different subdirectories**, set **Root Directory** to the directory of the app that project should build: **Settings → Build & Deployment → Root Directory → Save**. Vercel applies the change on the next deployment. If both apps need independent deployments, create a separate Vercel project for each app and set each project’s Root Directory accordingly; Vercel’s [monorepo guide](https://vercel.com/docs/monorepos) describes configuring projects for individual directories.

## If a production build fails, does the live URL keep working?

**For an existing project with a successful production deployment: normally, yes.** Vercel says production domains are updated to point to a new deployment **when that production deployment succeeds**. A failed build therefore does not replace the last successful production deployment; the failed deployment’s own URL is separate from the project’s production domain.

**Important first-deployment exception:** if the project has never had a successful production deployment, its production domains do not serve a deployment until one succeeds. Vercel explicitly notes this in [Environments](https://vercel.com/docs/deployments/environments).

### Sources

- [Configuring a Build](https://vercel.com/docs/builds/configure-a-build) — dashboard Framework Preset, per-deployment `vercel.json` override, Root Directory steps.
- [Programmatic Configuration with `vercel.ts`](https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/vercel-ts) — framework override, valid slugs including `vite` and `nextjs`, and `null` for Other.
- [Using Monorepos](https://vercel.com/docs/monorepos) — selecting a project’s Root Directory.
- [Environments](https://vercel.com/docs/deployments/environments) — when production domains update and the first-production-deployment exception.
- [Deploying to Vercel](https://vercel.com/docs/deployments) — deployment status and details shown in the dashboard."}]}

**Problem 1 — wrong framework preset.** Your project was created as a Vite app, so Vercel kept building a Next.js codebase with the Vite preset. I pinned it with [vercel.json](vercel.json) (`framework: "nextjs"`, `buildCommand: "next build"`), deleted the leftover Vite entry files `index.html` and `vite.config.ts`, untracked the 84 committed `.next` build-artifact files, and updated [.gitignore](.gitignore) and [README.md](README.md).

> `Vulnerable version of Next.js detected, please update immediately`
> `Build cache cleared after a dependency security block. Redeploy to build with a clean cache.`
> `status ● Error`

`next@15.2.4` is affected by **CVE-2025-66478** (CVSS 10.0 remote-code-execution in the React Server Components protocol — the "React2Shell" advisory), so Vercel flatly refuses to publish it. That's the "Action Required: critical vulnerabilities" banner in your dashboard, and it's why your dashboard kept saying production was the **Oct 23 deployment**: every build since the redesign died at the last step, and a failed build never moves your domain. Your code was never broken — the "syntax error in contact page" commit was chasing a ghost.

```tsx
useLayoutEffect(() => {
  const el = itemRefs.current[activeHref]

  if (!el || !list) return
  const measure = () => {
    const b = el.getBoundingClientRect(); const l = list.getBoundingClientRect()

  }
  measure()
  window.addEventListener('resize', measure)
  const t = setTimeout(measure, 250) // after fonts/layout settle
  return () => { window.removeEventListener('resize', measure); clearTimeout(t) }
}, [activeHref])
```

/**
 * Floating bottom dock — mobile only (hidden from 761px up, where the
 * header nav takes over).
 *
 * The active chip is a single absolutely-positioned element that slides
 * between items: its x/width are measured only when the route changes or
 * the viewport resizes — never on scroll — and CSS carries the motion with
 * an overshoot easing, so it glides like a spring without a per-frame loop.
 */
export function BottomNav() {
  const pathname = usePathname()
  const listRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const itemRefs = useRef<Record<string, HTMLAnchorElement | null>>({})
  const [chip, setChip] = useState({ x: 0, w: 0, ready: false })

  const activeHref = pathname === '/' ? '/' : pathname.replace(/\/+$/, '')

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const el = itemRefs.current[activeHref]
    const list = listRef.current
    if (!el || !list) return

    const measure = () => {
      const box = el.getBoundingClientRect()
      const base = list.getBoundingClientRect()
      setChip({ x: box.left - base.left, w: box.width, ready: true })
    }

    measure()
    // re-measure once fonts/layout have settled, and on every resize
    const t = window.setTimeout(measure, 250)
    window.addEventListener('resize', measure)
    return () => {
      window.clearTimeout(t)
      window.removeEventListener('resize', measure)
    }
  }, [activeHref])

  return (
    <nav className="mdock" aria-label="Primary">
      <div className="mdock__pill" ref={listRef}>
        <span
          className="mdock__chip"
          aria-hidden="true"
          style={{ transform: `translateX(${chip.x}px)`, width: chip.w, opacity: chip.ready ? 1 : 0 }}
        />
        {ITEMS.map((item, i) => {
          const active = item.href === activeHref
          return (
            <Link
              key={item.href}
              href={item.href}
              ref={(el) => {
                itemRefs.current[item.href] = el
              }}
              className={`mdock__item${active ? ' is-active' : ''}`}
              aria-label={item.label}
              title={item.label}
              aria-current={active ? 'page' : undefined}
              style={{ '--i': i } as React.CSSProperties}
            >
              <span className="mdock__icon" aria-hidden="true">
                {item.icon}
              </span>
            </Link>
          )
        })}
      </div>

      <Link
        href="/contact"
        className={`mdock__fab${activeHref === '/contact' ? ' is-active' : ''}`}
        aria-label="Talk to us"
        title="Talk to us"
      >
        {chatIcon}
      </Link>
    </nav>
  )
}
"}}

+/**
+ * Floating bottom dock — mobile only (hidden from 761px up, where the
+ * header nav takes over).
+ *
+ * The active chip is a single absolutely-positioned element that slides
+ * between items: its x/width are measured only when the route changes or
+ * the viewport resizes — never on scroll — and CSS carries the motion with
+ * an overshoot easing, so it glides like a spring without a per-frame loop.
+ */
+export function BottomNav() {
+  const pathname = usePathname()
+  const listRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
+  const itemRefs = useRef<Record<string, HTMLAnchorElement | null>>({})
+  const [chip, setChip] = useState({ x: 0, w: 0, ready: false })
+
+  const activeHref = pathname === '/' ? '/' : pathname.replace(/\/+$/, '')
+
+  useLayoutEffect(() => {
+    const el = itemRefs.current[activeHref]
+    const list = listRef.current
+    if (!el || !list) return
+
+    const measure = () => {
+      const box = el.getBoundingClientRect()
+      const base = list.getBoundingClientRect()
+      setChip({ x: box.left - base.left, w: box.width, ready: true })
+    }
+
+    measure()
+
+    // The item's entrance animation scales it (0.85 → 1), so its box is wrong
+    // while that runs — re-measure the moment it ends.
+    const onAnimationEnd = () => measure()

import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react'

type Blob = { x: number; y: number; r: number; color: string; ax: number; ay: number; sx: number; sy: number; ph: number }

/**
 * Calm animated backdrop — an organic gradient-mesh "fog" drawn on a 2D canvas.
 *
 * This is the light-weight stand-in for Vanta.js: Vanta's Fogs/Net effects run
 * on Three.js, which is heavy to ship and expensive on mobile GPUs, so we get
 * the same serene drifting-mist feel for a few KB with plain canvas 2D.
 *
 * Performance & accessibility safeguards:
 * - `prefers-reduced-motion` → paints one static frame, no rAF loop at all.
 * - Small screens → fewer blobs, device-pixel-ratio capped at 1, and the loop
 *   is throttled to ~30fps (motion is ambient; nobody will notice the delta).
 * - Desktop → DPR capped at 1.5, ~60fps.
 * - The loop pauses entirely while the tab is hidden and is cancelled on
 *   unmount, so no timers or frames leak between routes.
 */
export function AmbientBackground() {
  const canvasRef = useRef<HTMLCanvasElement>(null)

  useEffect(() => {
    const canvas = canvasRef.current
    if (!canvas) return
    const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d', { alpha: true })
    if (!ctx) return

    const reduced = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches
    const small = window.innerWidth < 700
    const dp [… 271 characters omitted] fff1c9']

      x: Math.random(),
      y: Math.random(),
      r: 0.18 + Math.random() * 0.22,
      color: palette[i % palette.length],
      ax: 0.04 + Math.random() * 0.07, // drift amplitude (x)
      ay: 0.05 + Math.random() * 0.08, // drift amplitude (y)
      sx: 0.00004 + Math.random() * 0.00006, // drift speed (x)
      sy: 0.00005 + Math.random() * 0.00007, // drift speed (y)
      ph: Math.random() * Math.PI * 2,
    }))

    let w = 0
    let h = 0
    let raf = 0
    let last = 0
    let alive = true

    const resize = () => {
      w = Math.max(1, Math.floor(window.innerWidth * dpr))
      h = Math.max(1, Math.floor(window.innerHeight * dpr))
      canvas.width = w
      canvas.height = h
      if (reduced) paint(0)
    }

    /** Draw one frame of drifting mist. `t` is a timestamp in ms. */
    const paint = (t: number) => {
      ctx.clearRect(0, 0, w, h)
      for (const b of blobs) {
        const cx = (b.x + Math.sin(t * b.sx + b.ph) * b.ax) * w
        const cy = (b.y + Math.cos(t * b.sy + b.ph) * b.ay) * h
        const r = b.r * Math.max(w, h)
        const g = ctx.createRadialGradient(cx, cy, 0, cx, cy, r)
        g.addColorStop(0, b.color + 'b3') // ~70% alpha core
        g.addColorStop(1, b.color + '00') // fully faded edge
        ctx.fillStyle = g
        ctx.beginPath()
        ctx.arc(cx, cy, r, 0, Math.PI * 2)
        ctx.fill()
      }
    }

    const loop = (t: number) => {
      if (!alive) return
      raf = requestAnimationFrame(loop)
      if (t - last < frameGap) return
      last = t
      paint(t)
    }

    const onVisibility = () => {
      if (document.hidden) {
        cancelAnimationFrame(raf)
      } else if (!reduced && alive) {
        raf = requestAnimationFrame(loop)
      }
    }

    resize()
    if (!reduced) raf = requestAnimationFrame(loop)
    window.addEventListener('resize', resize)
    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', onVisibility)

    return () => {
      alive = false
      cancelAnimationFrame(raf)
      window.removeEventListener('resize', resize)
      document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', onVisibility)
    }
  }, [])

  return <canvas ref={canvasRef} className="ambient" aria-hidden="true" />

import { useState, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { animated, useSpring, config } from '@react-spring/web'

/**
 * Physics-based card hover (React Spring).
 *
 * Pointer enter/leave drives a spring on `y`/`scale`, so cards lift with an
 * organic settle instead of a mechanical CSS ease. Focus/blur mirror hover for
 * keyboard users. Springs clean themselves up on unmount (hook-owned).
 */
export function SpringCard({ children, className, lift = 7 }: { children: ReactNode; className?: string; lift?: number }) {
  const [hovered, setHovered] = useState(false)

  const style = useSpring({
    y: hovered ? -lift : 0,
    scale: hovered ? 1.022 : 1,
    config: { tension: 280, friction: 18 }, // slightly springy settle
    reset: true,
  })

  return (
    <animated.article
      className={className}
      style={style}
      onPointerEnter={() => setHovered(true)}
      onPointerLeave={() => setHovered(false)}
      onFocus={() => setHovered(true)}
      onBlur={() => setHovered(false)}
    >
      {children}
    </animated.article>
  )
}

/**
 * Gentle idle float for decorative layers (hero orbs/sun).
 *
 * A spring oscillation between `-distance` and `distance` with `loop.reverse`
 * gives a calm breathing bob. Nest it *inside* a parallax wrapper if the same
 * element also needs GSAP scrub — two systems, two elements, no transform
 * collisions.
 */
export function Float({
  children,
  className,
  distance = 10,
  duration = 3400,
}: {
  children: ReactNode
  className?: string
  distance?: number
  duration?: number
}) {
  const style = useSpring({
    from: { y: -distance },
    to: { y: distance },
    loop: { reverse: true },
    config: { duration, easing: (t) => t * (2 - t) }, // easeInOutSine-like, no overshoot
  })

  return (
    <animated.div className={className} style={style} aria-hidden="true">
      {children}
    </animated.div>
  )
}

/**
 * Infinite, pause-on-hover marquee.

 * Two identical rows sit inside one track that translates from 0 to -50% —
 * because the halves are pixel-identical the wrap point is seamless, and the
 * animation is a single compositor-only `transform` (no layout, no JS loop), so
 * it holds 60fps for free.

      <div className="marquee__track">
        {row(false)}
        {row(true)}

}
